basis: Malignancy of mature lymphoid blood cells; lymphoma warrants the immune axis. Extranodal organs vary across subtypes.
Orofacial cleft is a congenital structural defect of the mouth, including the lip or palate; no additional organ involvement is established.
Hereditary reduction of an immunoglobulin is an immune-system abnormality; no associated organ damage is supplied.
Motor-neuron degeneration defines ALS; frontotemporal dementia is also neurologic. Muscle wasting reflects denervation.
Pigmentary lesions and peptic/hiatal disease define the syndrome; myopia occurs in 80-99%. Type 2 diabetes is treated as a separate disease.
Congenital urethral duplication affects the urinary tract; associated anorectal structural anomalies occur in 30-79%. Urinary infections are occasional.
Localized retinal capillary and neuroretinal disease causes progressive central visual loss; systemic vascular involvement is not established.
Destructive granulomatous thyroid inflammation causes thyroid dysfunction; a presumed viral trigger does not establish infection or autoimmune disease.
Skeletal deformities, skeletal-muscle disease and neurological defects are defining features; unspecified sensory defects do not establish another axis.
Premature fusion of all cranial sutures is a skeletal malformation; neurological or visual damage is not established as common.
Skeletal and dental anomalies define CCD2; developmental delay occurs in 3/6. Hearing impairment in 2/7 (~29%) is included at the approximate 30% boundary.
Hypoplastic or absent distal phalanges and nails define the syndrome; both skeletal and nail abnormalities are very frequent.
Craniosynostosis and digital skeletal malformations define type 1. Proptosis and high palate alone do not establish functional injury; hearing loss is occasional.
Inherited sinus-node dysfunction causes cardiac conduction and rhythm abnormalities; syncope does not establish neurological damage.
Glycosylation disorder; neurological injury includes delay, seizures and cerebral atrophy (1/1); liver dysfunction and coagulation abnormalities occur in 30-79%.
Calvarial hyperostotic lesions, low bone density and recurrent fractures define skeletal disease. Hearing impairment is reported in only 1-4%.
Inherited bronchiectasis directly damages the airways. Elevated sweat chloride alone does not establish a systemic electrolyte or endocrine disorder.
Periostosis, arthropathy and pachydermia define PHO; eyelid thickening produces ptosis in 30-79%. GI symptoms alone do not establish damage; ulcers are occasional.
Benign peripheral nerve-sheath tumour in the posterior mediastinum; its location does not establish lung or cardiac involvement.
Tumour originates in the respiratory mucosa of the maxillary sinus, which belongs to the airway axis.
Inhaled household antigens provoke immune-mediated inflammation of the lung parenchyma; no common extrapulmonary damage is established.
Ischaemic necrosis of anterior or anterolateral myocardium directly damages the heart.
Autoimmune inflammation directly damages blood vessels; specific downstream organs are not consistently affected across this umbrella concept.
Mitochondrial metabolic disease; encephalopathy, cardiomyopathy and optic atrophy each occur in 2/2. Muscle atrophy and hearing loss each 1/2 are omitted under the cap.
Developmental brain malformations and developmental delay define disease; microphthalmia and retinal dysplasia are each reported in 1/3 (~33%).
